overview: The committee reviewed the first draft of the Boston Avenue corridor rezoning proposal and the institutional zoning framework for Tufts University. The council voted to prohibit certain drive-through uses and referred the amended draft for a joint meeting with the Community Development Board.

items.title: Boston Avenue Rezoning Presentation
items.summary: Emily Innes presented a draft rezoning plan for the Boston Avenue corridor, proposing three mixed-use sub-districts focused on transit-oriented development near Green Line stations.

items.title: District Naming and Use Table Amendments
items.summary: The committee agreed to rename the sub-districts BA1, BA2, and BA3; the council approved an amendment to prohibit drive-through restaurants and gas stations in all three districts.

items.title: Dimensional Standards and Incentive Heights
items.summary: Councilors debated height limits and recommended a base of three stories for BA1, four for BA2, and six for BA3, with incentives allowing maximum heights of four, seven, and eight stories respectively.

items.title: Green Scores and Environmental Requirements
items.summary: The proposal increases the 'green score' requirement to 25 points to incentivize larger trees and bioswales in comparison to the Medford Square standards.

items.title: Tufts University Institutional Zoning
items.summary: The committee discussed a framework for a new institutional zone covering the Tufts campus, including sub-areas for campus core versus residential-facing properties.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: Residents expressed concerns regarding excessive building heights, potential shadow impacts on the Hillside neighborhood, and the definition of private versus university-owned dormitories.

items.title: Committee Referral
items.summary: Referred the amended Boston Avenue rezoning proposal to the full City Council for a joint discussion with the Community Development Board.
